title: Seek the peace of the city (Jeremiah 29:4–7)
hookLine: a letter to the exiles: build houses, plant gardens, pray for the city you live in
carry: plant a garden there, and pray for the place
last: SILENCE TURNED OUT TO BE IMPOSSIBLE.

cards: A letter goes out from Jerusalem, carried by messengers, to people who have been taken away to Babylon: elders, priests, prophets, craftsmen, ordinary families.
They're living in the capital of the empire that conquered them. And some prophets among them are saying: don't unpack. This will be over soon.
Jeremiah's letter says something else, and to people who wanted to hear go home, it is a hard letter.

teach.b: Here's the heart of it. "Build ye houses, and dwell in them; and plant gardens, and eat the fruit of them." Houses are for staying.
Gardens take time to bear. Jeremiah is telling the exiles to stop waiting at the door. Marry, he goes on, have children, see your children married, increase there and don't dwindle.
Then the line that gives today its title.

teach.h: SEEK THE PEACE OF THE CITY.
teach.b: "And seek the peace of the city whither I have caused you to be carried away captives, and pray unto the LORD for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace." The city is Babylon, the power that conquered Jerusalem.
And the exiles are told to seek its shalom, its peace, its welfare, and to pray for it.

Not because Babylon deserves it, but because their lives are now tied to it: in its peace, your peace. Later in the chapter the letter promises a return, but not soon. Until then, live fully where you are.
A related teaching appears in the Mishnah.

teach.h: PRAY FOR THE WELFARE OF THE GOVERNMENT.
teach.b: Pirkei Avot records Rabbi Chanina, the deputy high priest, saying: pray for the welfare of the government, for without fear of it, people would swallow one another alive.
And synagogue prayer books include a prayer for the country and its government, said on Shabbat.
Jeremiah's letter asked something hard of people living somewhere they never chose: plant a garden there, and pray for the place.

how: In synagogue, a prayer for the welfare of the country and its government is said on Shabbat morning after the Torah reading, carrying forward Jeremiah's instruction to seek the peace of the city.

games.q: you've been carried off to the city that conquered your home. a letter arrives from Jeremiah. what does it say?
o: resist the city at every turn.
build, plant, and seek the city's peace.
wait at the gate; you'll be home soon.
games.why: seek the peace of the city, and pray for it: for in the peace thereof shall ye have peace.

practice: Bring your town or city to mind, the actual streets, and pick one place: the bus stop, the corner store, the school, the clinic, the park.
Think of the people who work there and the people who need it, and ask what its peace needs right now. If you pray, you can hold Jeremiah's words for it; if you don't, hold the wish.

wordCard.voice: shalom, the peace Jeremiah told the exiles to seek for Babylon, the city that conquered them, and to pray for: for in its peace is yours. Today's word.
